R10-RECORD-API-BUDGET: M0, M1 and M2 of `dev/audit/rca/install-ratelimit.md`. M3 is not in this branch: decision O-1 makes it conditional on M0's measured limit, which only a push to main after this merges can print.

Governance's `record` job walked `<last v* tag>..origin/main` three times per push to main on the repository's `GITHUB_TOKEN` bucket: `--record`, `--stats` and `--sunset` each fetched the commit-to-PR map (W reads), and `--stats` and `--sunset` each fetched the per-PR reads (3P). That is 3W + 6P reads where W + 3P carry the same data.

- **M0** (`governance.yml` `record`): `gh api rate_limit` prints the core bucket as `RATE_LIMIT before:` (before the window walk) and `RATE_LIMIT after:` (after it, `always()`). `rate_limit` is not counted against the limit. `|| true` keeps it a log line, never a gate.
- **M1** (`policy_lint.mjs`): `--window-cache <file>`. The first mode to read a part of the window writes it and the later modes read it back. The file is keyed on the two resolved SHAs, so a file from another window or head is ignored. Only a complete read serves: a failed enumeration writes nothing, and an aborted per-PR fetch carries an empty map that serves no read, so every failure marker keeps its meaning. Each mode prints a `WINDOW_CACHE:` line saying what the file served. The job passes `"$RUNNER_TEMP/window.json"` to all three modes.
- **M2** (`governance.yml` `record`): `concurrency: {group: governance-record, cancel-in-progress: false}`. One run goes, one waits, and a newer push replaces the waiting one. The run that starts checks out main's newest tip, whose window holds every superseded push's.
- **Harness** (`dev/audit/harnesses/record_api_calls.sh`, the #2606 review carries): it passes `--window-cache` to a mode only when the job passes it to every invocation of that mode. It refuses (rc 1) a mode that printed a failure marker (enumeration skip, stats fetch guard, sunset `no friction data`, dead curl) and a `--record` zero over a window that holds first-parent commits.
- **Replay** (`dev/audit/harnesses/record_burst_replay.py`, new): replays a burst of pushes against the before, M1 and M1+M2 shapes. GitHub's group semantics are simulated, and a run measures the tip at its start.
- HANDOVER item 44 now names the `GITHUB_TOKEN` bucket, not an App quota, and says where its size is printed.

Alternatives (fixer.md step 17):
- One process running all three modes in memory would merge three steps whose failure semantics differ: `--record`'s exit code is the job's verdict, `--stats` and `--sunset` are `|| true`, and the friction filer runs between them on `stats.txt`.
- A URL-keyed `ghGet` disk cache would reach every caller of `ghGet`, including `--pr-body`'s red-history walk, which must read live.
- So: the RCA's `--window-cache`, scoped to the three window modes.

## Head

`b295569653015308aec95e267f5f750998447e5c` merges main `e30b24b` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`b7d2b645faf0a440f269b5734d16025058d53e61` merges the authored code head `63a4dce67a01c7a3289e3275f01a800a0d94efbf` and then merges origin/main `e364a0d73` (an automatic merge by the orchestrator's script; any resolution inside the code head is described below) into this PR's previous head.

Round 2: `63a4dce67a01c7a3289e3275f01a800a0d94efbf` is the merge of `origin/main` (`d6308d77` and later) into the commit `e1ff812cebd05ff80a5519d217c886ff89348892`, which adds one commit to the reviewed head `3fd42d9539ee90e5bf409593ff681f748db76f6e` and answers the round-1 block (`unpinned-site`). `e1ff812` changes `tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs` (two acceptance arms) and `tests/entities.py` (two checks). The merge conflicted in `dev/programme/rosters/wave-r10-groups.json` and took main's version, so this diff does not edit the roster (`git diff origin/main...HEAD -- dev/programme/rosters` is empty). Steps 2-8 were re-run on the merged tree.

Round 1 head: `3fd42d9539ee90e5bf409593ff681f748db76f6e` adds one commit to the previous head, containing only this PR's own row, `dev/programme/delivery/2629.md`. The authored code head is `a3e0d489d592b9800f4fad97c23c6871284275cd`.

`28e5d9c1652d273eb94b1f33390037baf074d785` merges origin/main `de69745ff` into the authored code head `a3e0d489d592b9800f4fad97c23c6871284275cd` (an automatic merge by the orchestrator's script; any resolution inside the code head is described below).

a3e0d489d592b9800f4fad97c23c6871284275cd. The base is fd9914851f063bc03bb44d4050ad30d6d0052f8d, as dispatched. origin/main was at de69745ff when this was written (2026-10-22T21:28Z) and touches none of this branch's files except an auto-mergeable `tests/closures.json` line.

## Mutation proof

Each mutant was run in the scratch replay clone described under `## Figures`, scored by the head's acceptance (`node tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs`) and by `record_api_calls.sh v7.0.2`:

| mutant | harness TOTAL | acceptance |
|---|---|---|
| M-A `readWindowCache` returns `{}` (the per-mode fetch restored) | 834 | rc=1, `FIXTURE VACUOUS: window cache` with 5 arms: map fetched 2 times; per-PR reads fetched 3 times; `--record`, `--stats` and `--sunset --window-cache did not take ... from the file` |
| M-B a cache missing a pull request serves the read (`if (cached)`) | 370 | rc=1, 2 arms: per-PR reads fetched 1 time; the null control |
| M-C `cmdStats` enumeration not given the cache | 464 | rc=1, `--stats --window-cache did not take commit-to-PR map and per-PR reads from the file` |
| M-D `cmdSunset` per-PR reads not given the cache | 646 | rc=1, `--sunset --window-cache did not take ...` |
| M-E the commit-to-PR map never written | 558 | rc=1, `the commit-to-PR map was fetched 2 time(s) for two reads of one window, not once` |

Round 2 answers the block's survivors. Each row failed on its mutant and passed on the fix; the fix reads `FIXTURE ok: 92 error(s) hold 253 pins` at rc=0 and `ALL ... ENTITY CHECKS` lists both new checks as `ok`.

| mutant (round-1 name) | scored by | result |
|---|---|---|
| R1 `pullsByShaShared` writes a failed enumeration as an empty map | acceptance | rc=1, `FIXTURE VACUOUS: window cache` with 2 arms: a failed commit-to-PR enumeration was cached or served; a read after a failed enumeration did not fetch for itself |
| R1b the `if (fetched.ok)` guard deleted | acceptance | uncaught `TypeError` on `[...undefined]`, `node tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs` rc=1 (round 1: rc=0) |
| R2 `readWindowCache` returns `cache || {}` (key check dropped) | acceptance | rc=1, `a window cache keyed on another window was served instead of ignored` |
| M1-yaml every `--window-cache "$RUNNER_TEMP/window.json"` removed from the `record` job | `tests/entities.py` | `every record-job invocation of --record, --stats and --sunset passes the same --window-cache file` FAIL, arguments `[()]` |
| Y1 only the `--sunset` `.claude` arm loses the flag | `tests/entities.py` | the same check FAIL, arguments `[(), ('"$RUNNER_TEMP/window.json"',)]` |

The new acceptance arms are a failing `pulls` stand-in read twice (must fetch twice and leave no file, then a good fetch must be fetched, not served) and two files seeded with a foreign key, one read for the commit-to-PR map and one for the per-PR reads. The new `tests/entities.py` checks read the `record` job's text: the first asserts all five invocations are found (`record` 1, `stats` 2, `sunset` 2, the null control that the pattern reads something), the second that every one passes the same `"$RUNNER_TEMP/window.json"`. R1, R1b and R2 were applied to `policy_lint.mjs` and restored from a saved copy; the YAML mutants were applied to the committed `governance.yml` and restored by `git checkout`; `git status` was clean after each. The entities mutants ran the whole script (about 4 minutes each).

The fixed tree reads 370 with acceptance rc=0. Removing the job's flag also moves the harness: dropping `--window-cache` from the `--record` invocation reads 464, and from either `--stats` invocation reads 740.

One mutant was equivalent and its code is gone. An earlier draft guarded the per-PR write with `if (!out.fetchError)`, and deleting that guard survived both instruments. The reason: a failed fetch carries an empty map, which serves no read. The guard was dead, so it was removed rather than triaged.

## Null control

- **Empty window:** `record_api_calls.sh origin/main` reads `TOTAL 0` at both ends.
- **No `--window-cache`:** each mode prints `WINDOW_CACHE: off -- ...` and fetches as before (the acceptance's null-control arms).
- **Harness carries:** with origin set to a non-GitHub URL, the base harness printed `TOTAL 0` at rc=0, and the head harness refuses with the `merge-enumeration` skip at rc=1. With a stub answering HTTP 403 on `pulls/N`, the head harness refuses `--stats` as partial at rc=1, quoting the fetch guard.

## Figures

- **The window cache, fixed window.** `bash dev/audit/harnesses/record_api_calls.sh v7.0.2` (sha1 ea6faad3f767) reads 834 at the base and 370 at the head. Rule: one line per REST call the stub curl logs, summed over the job's three modes. Run in a scratch clone of this head whose `refs/remotes/origin/main` is pinned to 04c1dd779 (the RCA's measuring point) with a GitHub origin URL. The base row used the base's own harness and `policy_lint.mjs`. Head: `--record 94`, `--stats 276`, `--sunset 0`, so W + 3P = 94 + 3×92. Base: 94 + 370 + 370. The total on today's window is a sliding figure, so it is not stated: re-run the same command at your own main.
- **Run count after M1+M2.** `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/record_burst_replay.py v7.0.2 2026-10-22T08:00:00Z 2026-10-22T09:00:00Z` (sha1 4113f53a91a3), at this head:
  - before: 6 runs, 4,599 calls. This reproduces the RCA's ≈ 4,600 and is the replay's control.
  - M1: 6 runs, 2,040 calls.
  - M1+M2: 4 runs, 1,364 calls with a run overhead of 30 or 60 s, and 4 runs, 1,368 calls at 120 s. A 240 s overhead gives 3 runs, 1,026 calls.
  - Rule: a push is a first-parent commit of origin/main timed by committer date. A run costs the W + 3P of the tip at its start and lasts the overhead plus 0.42 s per call; the 0.42 s/call is the RCA's reading of run 39755501453. The overhead is swept because no offline instrument reads it.
  - The #2606 review's "about 5 runs, 1,850" is not what the replay reads.
  - Same command for the 06Z hour: before 4,305; M1+M2 4 runs, 1,277 to 1,281 at 30 to 120 s.
  - Same command for the 09Z hour: 5 runs and 1,810 calls in every row. The pushes there are spaced wider than a run, so the group coalesces nothing. That is the replay's null control: it does not invent coalescing.
- **The replay agrees with the harness:** its W + 3P at tip 04c1dd779 is 94 + 3×92 = 370, the harness's head total above.
- **Demand against the limit:** about 1,364 calls in the worst replayed hour after M1+M2, compared with a `GITHUB_TOKEN` limit nobody has measured. Run 39745228063's ≈ 3,000 calls in 4 minutes (the brief) is above 1,000/hr, so the record's 1,000 is not the limit. Whether M3 is owed is O-1's call on M0's first reading, carried below.
- **Acceptance:** `node tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs`: `FIXTURE ok: 92 error(s) hold 253 pins` at the head, 246 at the base. The 7 new pins are the window-cache block: 5 in round 1, 2 in round 2.
- **Gate scope:** `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD) --workdir "$D"` printed `MODE: SCOPED -- 2 script(s) run, 31 scoped out` (`tests/entities.py`, `tests/harness_headers.py`).
  - `tests/entities.py`: 2401 checks at the merged head (2399 at `e1ff812`). `tests/doc_claims.py` printed `ALL 203 checks PASSED` at `e1ff812`; at the merged head the scoped gate names `tests/entities.py` and `tests/harness_headers.py` only (`MODE: SCOPED -- 2 script(s) run, 31 scoped out`). Both new checks print `ok`. The run on this Mac (Python 3.14, `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub`) reports `4 of 2401 ENTITY CHECKS FAILED`, all in the heartbeat py-spy control (`hb:`: its retry, rest and `HB_CONTROL_TRIES` checks), which this diff does not touch and which depends on `py-spy` on this host; CI is the authority for that one. Round 1 read `ALL 2397 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED` under Python 3.13.
  - `tests/harness_headers.py`: `ALL 109 HARNESS HEADER CHECKS PASSED`.
  - Both ran under Python 3.13 with `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub`.
- **run_always:**
  - `tests/structure.py`: `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED` (round 2).
  - `python3 tests/mutation_table.py --pin-killed --base origin/main`: `scope changed: no production code line added or modified against the base`, `0 new unpinned site(s)`, `PIN KILLED: nothing to pin`, 4062 unpinned at both ends. The table's scope is `custom_components`; this diff adds no line there.
  - `node tools/policy/policy_lint_mutants.mjs`: `MUTANTS ok` (round 2).
  - `tests/layout.py`: `layout self-test: ok`.
  - `tests/closure.py selftest`: `ALL 112 closure shrink pins PASSED`.
  - `tests/env_drift.py --claims-only <merge base>`: `claims hygiene: ... ok`.
- **Policy lanes:**
  - `node tools/policy/policy_lint_envmatrix.mjs "$PWD" <work> HEAD`: `16 declared outcome(s) held, 0 did not, across 6 environment shape(s)`.
  - `node tools/policy/policy_lint_mutants.mjs`: `MUTANTS ok`.
  - `node tools/policy/brief_lint.mjs`: `TOTAL: 0 error(s) across 47 file(s)`.
  - `node tools/policy/rules_sync.mjs --check`: ok.
  - `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/tmp_paths.py --check`: `0 refused`.
  - `python3 tools/audit/archscore/score.py --diff <merge base>`: `dS +0.0000 NULL`, because no Python production file changed.
- **Agreement lane, both copies** (the dispatch's instruction):
  - Branch copy: `python3 -I tools/policy/agreement_py.py --out <f>` then `node tools/policy/agreement.mjs --py-json <f>` gave `RESULT divergent=0 unregistered=0 dead=0 refused=0` and `AGREEMENT ok`.
  - Base copy: run in a worktree of this head after restoring wave-script's pinned list from fd9914851, exactly as that job's `Restore the check source from the base commit` step does (2 files differ from the branch: `tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs`, `dev/audit/harnesses/record_api_calls.sh`). `agreement_py --restore` reported `0 missing`. The lane gave `RESULT divergent=0 unregistered=0 dead=0 refused=0` and `AGREEMENT ok`; `check-wave-script.mjs` gave `202 passed, 0 failed`; the base copy of `policy_lint.mjs` over this tree gave `TOTAL: 0 error(s)` and `246 pins`.

## Unpinned sites

- Round 1 block, closed: the `record` job's `--window-cache` wiring is pinned by a check in `tests/entities.py` (M1-yaml and Y1 above). `pullsByShaShared`'s `if (fetched.ok)` write guard (R1, R1b) and `readWindowCache`'s key check (R2) are pinned by acceptance arms. None is a written triage.
- M0's two `rate_limit` steps and M2's `concurrency:` block are workflow YAML that no check reads. Disposition: a written triage. M0 is a log line whose deletion changes no verdict, so the RCA calls it a log line, not a gate. M2's effect is measured by the replay above. A pin on the group's text would pin a spelling and not the queueing GitHub does.

## Architecture score

n/a: no Python production file changed (`dS +0.0000 NULL`).

## Red checks

- **nightly-status**: it grades `main`, and this diff touches files it reads (`.github/workflows/governance.yml`, `docs/HANDOVER.md`), but the red is not this pull request's. No scheduled Nightly has concluded yet. The workflow is younger than its first cron slot, about 2026-10-23T02:17Z, so the check reads a false ABSENT on every head, `main` included. That defect is R10-NIGHTLY-ABSENT, fixed by #2627. This diff changes neither the Nightly workflow nor `tests/nightly_status.py`. The cheaper detector is the one #2627 lands, a NEW/ABSENT fixture pair driven by `fast` through `tests/entities.py`. Its standing cost is milliseconds.
- **pr-contract**, round 1: `carry_audit.py check --body` refused with 4 unrouted items, because the `Carry:` values of `## Forward-carry` and `## Friction` were not `<GROUP> | #<issue> | O<n> | dismissed: <reason>` destinations. Routing them is the roster seat's body patch (`body_patch.sh`); this round's body keeps whatever `Carry:` lines the live body held when it was built (none had been changed at build time), and does not re-word them.
- **pr-contract**, round 0: the first head had no delivery row, because the opener's row push was refused on the unanswered nightly-status red above. The row lands with this body.

## Forward-carry

- **M3's inputs, for decision O-1:** where M0's limit is read (`RATE_LIMIT before:`/`after:` in the `record` log), how demand after M1+M2 is re-measured (`dev/audit/harnesses/record_burst_replay.py` at the deciding seat's main), and that the #2606 review's 5-run estimate is not the replay's figure. Landed on `handoff/audit-r10-roster` at `1eee009fddc97111d5938174ba1f23659586a8da`. Carry: R10-RECORD-API-BUDGET
- **HANDOVER item 44's correction** (the brief's "at merge"). Carry: dismissed: the correction is made in this diff itself (HANDOVER.md item 44 now names the GITHUB_TOKEN bucket); no later stage owes it

## Friction

- tools/pr/prepr.sh: cost: its agreement lane runs the branch copy only, so the base-copy run the dispatch asked for was hand-built from wave-script's restore step. It took about 5 minutes and one wrong pass, because `governance.yml` holds three `Restore the check source from the base commit` steps and the first match is not wave-script's. Landed on `handoff/audit-r10-roster` at `f664d7b5d9e71a04f79c14f329ef572545a6309e`. Carry: R10-FLOW-JIDOKA
- tools/audit/seat/seat_venv.sh: stale: `uv` has no download for the cpython-3.14.7 the typing census records, so the seat venv cannot build in this container. The gate ran under the system Python 3.13 with `tests/requirements-ci.txt` installed without hashes. Landed on `handoff/audit-r10-roster` at `51d9ddc631d5295afbbda05991fcfbd26acedea0`, under R10-FLY-CLOUD-SETUP-TOOLCHAIN, the owner the re-cut gave this file. Carry: R10-FLY-CLOUD-SETUP-TOOLCHAIN

Fix review: blocked 3fd42d9539ee90e5bf409593ff681f748db76f6e unpinned-site: the job's --window-cache wiring and two cache guards survive every check and the body dispositions none of them

bus-nonce: 5c5034eb7c7f033d16bcd621330debde

Round 1. Head 3fd42d9539ee90e5bf409593ff681f748db76f6e was measured, and it was still the branch head when this verdict was written. Worktree detached at the head. `dev/governance/roles/` has no diff between the merge base and origin/main, so the contract I followed is current.

## Block

- **The M1 wiring in the workflow is pinned by nothing, and `## Unpinned sites` does not list it** (fixer.md step 2). I dropped every `--window-cache "$RUNNER_TEMP/window.json"` from governance.yml's `record` job (mutant `M1-yaml`, ev/mutants2.txt). The policy_lint acceptance still printed `FIXTURE ok ... 251 pins` at rc=0, `tests/entities.py` passed at rc=0, and `check-wave-script.mjs` printed `202 passed`. The same happened when I dropped only the `.claude` arm of `--sunset` (mutant `Y1`, ev/mutants.txt: acceptance rc=0). The head's `record_api_calls.sh` does see both: 834 and 740. But no CI lane runs that harness, so main can lose the 834→370 saving silently. The acceptance's "wiring" arm runs `policy_lint.mjs` by hand with the flag. It never reads the job text. The body's `## Unpinned sites` covers only M0's `rate_limit` steps and M2's `concurrency:` block.
- **Two guards the body names as properties survive the acceptance and the harness, and neither is dispositioned:**
  - `pullsByShaShared`'s `if (fetched.ok)` write guard ("a failed enumeration writes nothing"). Mutant `R1b` deletes the guard and mutant `R1` caches a failed enumeration as an empty map. Under both, the acceptance stays at rc=0 with 251 pins and the harness at 370. Every acceptance arm feeds `okPulls`, and no arm feeds a failing commit-to-PR fetch. Under R1, a 403 in `--record`'s enumeration, which is the saturation case this PR exists for, reaches `--stats` and `--sunset` as an `api`-mode window with zero pull requests. Neither prints `enumSkipLine`, and `--sunset` judges rules against an empty friction map instead of `no friction data`. That is the silent-zero class #1050 closed. Under R1b, `--record` throws on `[...undefined]` instead. The per-PR half of the same claim is pinned: the `badReads` arm kills R3.
  - `readWindowCache`'s key check `cache.key === windowKey(since)` ("a file left from another window or another head is ignored rather than trusted"). Mutant `R2` makes it `cache || {}`. The acceptance stays at rc=0 and the harness at 370. No arm seeds a file with a foreign key.
- **pr-contract is red at this head, and the red is not this PR's nightly-status answer.** I read the latest run, job 120135698603, which started 22:54:12Z after the last workflow concluded at 22:53:55Z. It refuses in `carry_audit.py check --body` with `CARRY-AUDIT: 4 finding item(s): 0 routed, 4 unrouted`. The 4 unrouted items are the two `## Forward-carry` bullets and the two `## Friction` bullets. Their `Carry:` values (`` `dev/programme/rosters/...` ``, `` `dev/programme/HANDOVER.md` ``, `none`) are not destinations of the form `Carry: <GROUP> | #<issue> | O<n> | dismissed: <reason>`. The body's `## Red checks` answers pr-contract only for the earlier missing-row cause. A body edit fixes this without moving the head.

What clears the block:
- One acceptance arm with a failing `pulls` stand-in, followed by a re-read that must fetch again.
- One arm with a foreign-key file, which must not serve.
- Either a pin that reads the `record` job's three invocations for `--window-cache`, for example in `tests/entities.py` or the acceptance, or a written triage of that site in `## Unpinned sites`.
- Routed `Carry:` markers in the body.

## Findings

- M0 survives every check: I deleted both `GITHUB_TOKEN rate limit` steps, and the acceptance, entities.py and check-wave-script all stayed green (ev/mutants2.txt). The dispatch asks for each of M0, M1 and M2 to be caught by a check. The body dispositions M0 by a written triage, a form fixer.md step 2 allows: it is a log line, never a gate. Whether that triage satisfies O-1's need to read the limit is the orchestrator's call. Carry: R10-RECORD-API-BUDGET
- M2 survives every check: I deleted the `concurrency:` block, and the acceptance, entities.py and check-wave-script all stayed green (ev/mutants2.txt). The body's written triage says a pin would fix a spelling and not GitHub's queueing, and the replay measures the effect offline. Same dispatch bar as M0, same disposition. Carry: R10-RECORD-API-BUDGET
- The finder's harness at the base (`record_api_calls.sh` as of fd9914851) passes no flags to the modes, so it reads 834 at both ends and cannot see M1. The fixer extended it to read the job's flags. I disclose my own instrument here: `ev/finder_harness_cache.sh` is the base harness plus `--window-cache` on all three modes. It reads 370 at the head and 0 on the empty window. `record_burst_replay.py` is the fixer's own new instrument, not the finder's. Carry: dismissed: disclosed instrument provenance, no defect

## Evidence

- RESULT harness-base-at-base (finder's harness, origin/main pinned to 04c1dd779, `v7.0.2`): `--record 94`, `--stats 370`, `--sunset 370`, TOTAL 834, rc=0 (ev/harness.txt).
- RESULT harness-head-at-head (head harness): 94 + 276 + 0, TOTAL 370, rc=0. The base harness at the head also reads 834, because it passes no flags. My cache variant at the head reads 94 + 276 + 0 = 370, and 0 on `origin/main..origin/main` (ev/harness_cache.txt).
- W + 3P versus 3W + 6P, measured: W = 94 and P = 92. 94 + 3×92 = 370, and 3×94 + 6×92 = 834. Both match the body.
- The PR's named mutants under the acceptance (`node tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs`) and the head harness (ev/mutants.txt). Each one reproduced the body's figure and was killed at rc=1:

  | mutant | harness TOTAL |
  |---|---|
  | M-A (per-mode fetch restored) | 834 |
  | M-B | 370 |
  | M-C | 464 |
  | M-D | 646 |
  | M-E | 558 |

  My R3 (a failed per-PR fetch written as empty reads) and R4 (`--record` not given the cache, harness 464) were also killed.
- RESULT replay (`record_burst_replay.py v7.0.2`, at the head, ev/replay.txt). Every row matches the body:

  | hour | before | M1 | M1+M2, 30 to 120 s | M1+M2, 240 s |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 08Z | 6 runs, 4599 calls | 2040 calls | 4 runs, 1364 to 1368 calls | 3 runs, 1026 calls |
  | 06Z | 4305 calls | 1911 calls | 4 runs, 1277 to 1281 calls | 3 runs, 960 calls |
  | 09Z | 5 runs, 1810 calls in every M1 row | | | |

  The 09Z hour is the null control.
- Concurrency (item 3): the `record` job sets `concurrency: {group: governance-record, cancel-in-progress: false}` (parsed with PyYAML). With `cancel-in-progress: false`, GitHub never cancels a running job. It only replaces a pending one, before any step runs, so a run cannot be cut off mid-write by the group. No other workflow uses the group name. The `timeout-minutes: 10` is unchanged. `record` is in merge_train.py's `NOT_GATING`, so a superseded pending run that shows `cancelled` on a main commit gates nothing.
